subject: Clarify traffic envelope, p95/p99 targets, and streaming fallbacks (post-call)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orchid.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@orchid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify traffic envelope, p95/p99 targets, and streaming fallbacks (post-call)

Thanks for the call earlier, Lena + Samir — good alignment on the business goals and the performance bar you care about. Short recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short POC that compares our hosted API to your current provider.

Summary from today's call
- Goal: confirm end-to-end p95 and p99 latency targets for the chat product under production-like traffic. You mentioned wanting tighter p95 for user experience and a reasonable p99 for tail events.
- Primary constraints: streaming-first UX (chunked responses), concurrent session volume, and burst behavior during morning peak.
- Success criteria (proposal): p95 <= 300 ms and p99 <= 1.2 s for typical chat interactions at 90th percentile token length. We left the exact envelope for you to share (traffic mix / concurrency).

What we need from you (action items)
1) Traffic profile CSV with: avg QPS, peak sustained QPS, distribution of tokens per response, % streaming vs non-streaming — please attach sample (we discussed a 7-day slice).
2) Confirmation of the maximum concurrent sessions you need preserved during peak (you mentioned ~200 concurrent streaming sessions).
3) Any hard SLOs required for startup latency (first-chunk latency) vs overall completion latency.

Redwood proposed POC plan (high level)
- Ingest your traffic profile and run two side-by-side probes: Redwood hosted API vs your incumbent in your staging environment / test account.
- Measure client-observed end-to-end p95/p99, and also collect per-hop breakdown (network + proxy + token generation).
- Run two modes: (A) best-effort throughput (maximize served QPS) and (B) strict-latency routing (enforce p95 SLO, fall back to smaller quantized model where helpful).

Next steps / timeline
- If you can drop the traffic CSV by EOD Thu (Jun 3), Ben/engineering can provision and run an initial probe within 48 hours.
- We'll circulate an internal runbook and a short test harness (lightweight) to make the measurement reproducible.

Attachments: redwood_poc_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook outline).

Thanks — I assigned Ben and Jonas to lead the technical side after this note. We'll keep the experiment narrow and measurable.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orchid.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify traffic envelope, p95/p99 targets, and streaming fallbacks (post-call)

Thanks Naomi — attaching the traffic slice as discussed. High-level pieces:
- avg QPS (per endpoint): 45
- peak sustained QPS (15 min): 220
- percent streaming (clients open a websocket/stream for chunked responses): 62%
- tokens per response (distribution): median 64, 90th 240, 99th 600
- concurrency: we expect 180-220 concurrent streaming sessions during peak windows (US mornings)

Notes on latency expectations:
- For our chat product the UX requirement is "first-chunk start latency" <= 120 ms p95 (this is the user-perceived start).
- Full completion p95 target we can tolerate up to 300 ms; p99 should stay under 1.2 s as Naomi suggested.

We attached: orchid_traffic_profile.csv (7-day slice) — column headers are timestamp, endpoint, request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, client_rtt_ms.

We can give Redwood a staging API key and run tests against our staging ingress. Samir will coordinate access.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform, Orchid.ai
Attachment: orchid_traffic_profile.csv (CSV, ~62KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orchid.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@orchid.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify traffic envelope, p95/p99 targets, and streaming fallbacks (post-call)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the CSV, Lena — exactly what we needed. Proposed concrete POC schedule:
- Day 0 (today/Thu): ingest profile and validate schema; confirm staging key and test endpoints.
- Day 1 (Fri): run baseline probes against incumbent (you provide test harness or we run against staging).
- Day 3 (Mon): run Redwood hosted probe at same traffic envelope (both modes: best-effort and strict-latency).
- Day 4: deliver a short report with client-observed p95/p99, streaming first-chunk latency breakdown, and fallback behavior notes.

Operational asks from Orchid: staging API key + a short-lived service account with scoped access to create test sessions (no production data).

We plan to hand off to Jonas for the technical setup (test config, concurrency shaping, token-length buckets). We'll share the exact command line and minimal container for you to reproduce locally.

Attachments: redwood_poc_runbook_v1.pdf (updated), redwood-test-harness.tar.gz (script + small container).

—Ben
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orchid.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@orchid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify traffic envelope, p95/p99 targets, and streaming fallbacks (post-call)

Lena / Samir — quick technical clarifications so we can size kernels and choose routing/fallback policies correctly. (Quoting your note below for context.)

> "percent streaming: 62%"
> "tokens per response: median 64, 90th 240, 99th 600"
> "concurrency: 180-220 concurrent streaming sessions at peak"

Questions / assumptions:
1) Client RTT distribution: the CSV column client_rtt_ms — please confirm the 90th RTT you observe in US regions (we need this to separate network contribution vs server-side).
2) Max sequence length we should provision for (model context window) — are you using 2k or 4k contexts for the chat history? That changes KV cache memory and batching efficiency.
3) Do some requests require function/tool calling (i.e., additional external calls) — those can inflate end-to-end completion time.

What we'll do on our side in the probe:
- Instrument streaming first-chunk latency separately from completion latency. We will report p50/p95/p99 for both.
- Run a concurrency-shaped probe that ramps to 220 concurrent streaming sessions and sustains for 15 minutes, then spike tests to 300 for a 2-minute burst to see fallbacks.
- Compare two routing modes: low-latency routing (small quantized model + priority placement) and cost-optimized routing (higher throughput batching).

I've uploaded a lightweight harness and a reproducible script to the Drive link Naomi mentioned (redwood-test-harness.tar.gz includes a README). If you can grant the staging key and confirm the 90th RTT value, I can kick off environment prep today and run the baseline tomorrow morning (Mon).

Relevant link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/test-harness — contains the latency collector and the client-side instrumentation we use.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-test-harness.tar.gz (script + container, ~4MB)

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@orchid.ai>

Thanks everyone — confirming staging access and timeline.
- Staging API key: staging-key-ORCH-2027 (will send via secure channel to Ben).
- 90th RTT in our US region: ~48 ms (we're on a fast CDN).
- Context window: 4096 tokens for the chat we want tested.
- No function calls in the baseline workload (we'll run a separate slot for tool-calls).

We're comfortable with your proposed POC cadence. Primary acceptance criteria for the POC report:
- First-chunk p95 <= 120 ms (client-observed)
- Completion p95 <= 300 ms, completion p99 <= 1.2 s for the 90th token-length bucket (240 tokens)

Ben — we'll provision the staging key and send it in a separate email to the address you specify. Once you confirm you received the key, please kick off the incumbent baseline and then Redwood hosted probe as scheduled.

Appreciate the clarity — looking forward to the numbers.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Engineering Lead, Orchid.ai
